verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā sāriputto sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Sāriputta was staying near Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena yamakassa nāma bhikkhuno evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ hoti:
verses.english: Now at that time a mendicant called Yamaka had the following harmful misconception:

verses.pali: “tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā”ti.
verses.english: “As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, a mendicant who has ended the defilements is annihilated and destroyed when their body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death.”

verses.pali: Assosuṁ kho sambahulā bhikkhū yamakassa kira nāma bhikkhuno evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ hoti:
“tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā”ti.
Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā yamako tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā yamakena saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
verses.english: They went to Yamaka and exchanged greetings with him.

verses.pali: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ nisīdiṁsu. Ekamantaṁ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṁ yamakaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they sat down to one side and said to him,

verses.pali: “Saccaṁ kira te, āvuso yamaka, evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
verses.english: “Is it really true, Reverend Yamaka, that you have such a harmful misconception:

verses.pali: ‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, a mendicant who has ended the defilements is annihilated and destroyed when their body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death’?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ khvāhaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi:
verses.english: “Yes, reverends, that’s how I understand the Buddha’s teaching.”

verses.pali: ‘khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
“Mā, āvuso yamaka, evaṁ avaca, mā bhagavantaṁ abbhācikkhi. Na hi sādhu bhagavato abbhācikkhanaṁ. Na hi bhagavā evaṁ vadeyya:
verses.english: “Don’t say that, Yamaka! Don’t misrepresent the Buddha, for misrepresentation of the Buddha is not good. And the Buddha would not say that.”

verses.pali: ‘khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā’”ti.
Evampi kho āyasmā yamako tehi bhikkhūhi vuccamāno tatheva taṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ thāmasā parāmāsā abhinivissa voharati:
verses.english: But even though admonished by those mendicants, Yamaka obstinately stuck to that misconception and insisted on stating it.

verses.pali: “tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā”ti.

Yato kho te bhikkhū nāsakkhiṁsu āyasmantaṁ yamakaṁ etasmā pāpakā diṭṭhigatā vivecetuṁ, atha kho te bhikkhū uṭṭhāyāsanā yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṁ sāriputtaṁ etadavocuṁ:
verses.english: When those mendicants were unable to dissuade Yamaka from that misconception, they got up from their seats and went to see Venerable Sāriputta. They told him what had happened, and said,

verses.pali: “yamakassa nāma, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhuno evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā’ti.
Sādhāyasmā sāriputto yena yamako bhikkhu tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
verses.english: “May Venerable Sāriputta please go to the mendicant Yamaka out of sympathy.”

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā yamako tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā yamakena saddhiṁ sammodi …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā sāriputto āyasmantaṁ yamakaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then in the late afternoon, Venerable Sāriputta came out of retreat, went to Venerable Yamaka and exchanged greetings with him. Seated to one side he said to Yamaka:

verses.pali: “Saccaṁ kira te, āvuso yamaka, evarūpaṁ pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ uppannaṁ:
verses.english: “Is it really true, Reverend Yamaka, that you have such a harmful misconception:

verses.pali: ‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, a mendicant who has ended the defilements is annihilated and destroyed when their body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death’?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ khvāhaṁ, āvuso, bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā”ti.
verses.english: “Yes, reverend, that’s how I understand the Buddha’s teaching.”
They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’
What do you think, Reverend Yamaka?
Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to form?”
“Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to feeling?” …
Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies in relation to form?”
“Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies apart from form?”
“Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies in relation to feeling?” …

verses.pali: rūpaṁ … vedanaṁ … saññaṁ … saṅkhāre … viññāṇaṁ tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
verses.english: Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to one who has form?” … “… feeling?” … “… perception?” … “… choices?” … “… consciousness?”

verses.pali: ayaṁ so arūpī … avedano … asaññī … asaṅkhāro … aviññāṇo tathāgatoti samanupassasī”ti?
verses.english: Do you consider that the label ‘realized one’ applies to that one who is without form?” … “… feeling?” … “… perception?” … “… choices?” … “… consciousness?”

verses.pali: “Ettha ca te, āvuso yamaka, diṭṭheva dhamme saccato thetato tathāgate anupalabbhiyamāne, kallaṁ nu te taṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ:
verses.english: “In that case, Reverend Yamaka, since a realized one is not found by you as a genuine fact in this very life, is it cogent for you to declare:

verses.pali: ‘tathāhaṁ bhagavatā dhammaṁ desitaṁ ājānāmi, yathā khīṇāsavo bhikkhu kāyassa bhedā ucchijjati vinassati, na hoti paraṁ maraṇā’”ti?
verses.english: ‘As I understand the Buddha’s teaching, a mendicant who has ended the defilements is annihilated and destroyed when their body breaks up, and doesn’t exist after death.’?”

verses.pali: “Ahu kho me taṁ, āvuso sāriputta, pubbe aviddasuno pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ;
verses.english: “Reverend Sāriputta, in my ignorance, I used to have that misconception.

verses.pali: idañca panāyasmato sāriputtassa dhammadesanaṁ sutvā tañceva pāpakaṁ diṭṭhigataṁ pahīnaṁ, dhammo ca me abhisamito”ti.
verses.english: But now that I’ve heard the teaching from Venerable Sāriputta, I’ve given up that misconception, and I’ve comprehended the teaching.”
“Reverend Yamaka, suppose they were to ask you:

verses.pali: ‘yo so, āvuso yamaka, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā kiṁ hotī’ti?
verses.english: ‘When their body breaks up, after death, what happens to a perfected one, who has ended the defilements?’

verses.pali: Evaṁ puṭṭho tvaṁ, āvuso yamaka, kinti byākareyyāsī”ti?

verses.english: “Reverend, if they were to ask this,

verses.pali: ‘yo so, āvuso yamaka, bhikkhu arahaṁ khīṇāsavo so kāyassa bhedā paraṁ maraṇā kiṁ hotī’ti?

verses.english: What’s suffering has ceased and disappeared.
What’s suffering has ceased and disappeared.’
That’s how I’d answer such a question.”

verses.pali: Tena hāvuso yamaka, upamaṁ te karissāmi etasseva atthassa bhiyyoso mattāya ñāṇāya.
verses.english: Well then, I shall give you a simile to make the meaning even clearer.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, āvuso yamaka, gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo;
verses.english: Suppose there was a householder or householder’s son who was rich, with a lot of money and great wealth,

verses.pali: Tassa kocideva puriso uppajjeyya anatthakāmo ahitakāmo ayogakkhemakāmo jīvitā voropetukāmo.
verses.english: Then along comes a person who wants to harm, injure, and threaten him, and take his life.

verses.pali: ‘ayaṁ kho gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā aḍḍho mahaddhano mahābhogo;
verses.english: ‘This householder or householder’s son is rich, with a lot of money and great wealth,
It won’t be easy to take his life by force.
Why don’t I get close to him, then take his life?’

verses.pali: So taṁ gahapatiṁ vā gahapatiputtaṁ vā upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ vadeyya:
verses.english: So he goes up to that householder or householder’s son and says:

verses.pali: Tamenaṁ so gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā upaṭṭhāpeyya.
verses.english: They would serve that householder or householder’s son.

verses.pali: So upaṭṭhaheyya pubbuṭṭhāyī pacchānipātī kiṅkārapaṭissāvī manāpacārī piyavādī.
verses.english: They’d get up before him and go to bed after him, and be obliging, behaving nicely and speaking politely.

verses.pali: Tassa so gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā mittatopi naṁ saddaheyya;
verses.english: The householder or householder’s son would consider them as a friend

verses.pali: Yadā kho, āvuso, tassa purisassa evamassa:
verses.english: But when that person realizes that

verses.pali: ‘saṁvissattho kho myāyaṁ gahapati vā gahapatiputto vā’ti, atha naṁ rahogataṁ viditvā tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropeyya.
verses.english: they’ve gained the trust of the householder or householder’s son, then, when they know he’s alone, they’d take his life with a sharp knife.

verses.pali: yadā hi so puriso amuṁ gahapatiṁ vā gahapatiputtaṁ vā upasaṅkamitvā evaṁ āha:
verses.english: When that person went to the householder or householder’s son and offered to
serve him, weren’t they a killer then,

verses.pali: Yadāpi so upaṭṭhahati pubbuṭṭhāyī pacchānipātī kiṅkārapaṭissāvī manāpacārī piyavādī, tadāpi so vadhakova.
verses.english: And when they got up before him and went to bed after him, being obliging, behaving nicely and speaking politely, weren’t they a killer then,

verses.pali: Yadāpi naṁ rahogataṁ viditvā tiṇhena satthena jīvitā voropeti, tadāpi so vadhakova.
verses.english: And when, knowing he was alone, they took his life with a sharp knife, weren’t they a killer then,

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, āvuso, assutavā puthujjano ariyānaṁ adassāvī ariyadhammassa akovido ariyadhamme avinīto, sappurisānaṁ adassāvī sappurisadhammassa akovido sappurisadhamme avinīto
verses.english: “In the same way, an unlearned ordinary person has not seen the noble ones, and is neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve not seen true persons, and are neither skilled nor trained in the teaching of the true persons.

verses.pali: rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, rūpavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā rūpaṁ, rūpasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
verses.english: They regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, viññāṇavantaṁ vā attānaṁ; attani vā viññāṇaṁ, viññāṇasmiṁ vā attānaṁ.
verses.english: They regard consciousness as self, self as having consciousness, consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

verses.pali: So aniccaṁ rūpaṁ ‘aniccaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ nappajānāti.
verses.english: They don’t truly understand form—which is impermanent—as impermanent.
They don’t truly understand form—which is suffering—as suffering.
They don’t truly understand form—which is not-self—as not-self.
They don’t truly understand form—which is conditioned—as conditioned.
They don’t truly understand form—which is a killer—as a killer.
consciousness—which is a killer—as a killer.

verses.pali: So rūpaṁ upeti upādiyati adhiṭṭhāti ‘attā me’ti.
verses.english: They’re attracted to form, grasp it, and fixate on the thought, ‘my self’.
consciousness, grasp it, and fixate on the thought, ‘my self’.

verses.pali: Tassime pañcupādānakkhandhā upetā upādinnā dīgharattaṁ ahitāya dukkhāya saṁvattanti.
verses.english: And when you’ve gotten involved with and grasped these five grasping aggregates, they lead to your lasting harm and suffering.

verses.pali: Sutavā ca kho, āvuso, ariyasāvako ariyānaṁ dassāvī …pe… sappurisadhamme suvinīto
verses.english: A learned noble disciple has seen the noble ones, and is skilled and trained in the teaching of the noble ones. They’ve seen true persons, and are skilled and trained in the teaching of the true persons.

verses.pali: na rūpaṁ attato samanupassati, na rūpavantaṁ attānaṁ; na attani rūpaṁ, na rūpasmiṁ attānaṁ.
verses.english: They don’t regard form as self, self as having form, form in self, or self in form.

verses.pali: na viññāṇaṁ attato samanupassati, na viññāṇavantaṁ attānaṁ;
verses.english: consciousness as self, self as having consciousness,

verses.pali: na attani viññāṇaṁ, na viññāṇasmiṁ attānaṁ.
verses.english: consciousness in self, or self in consciousness.

verses.pali: So aniccaṁ rūpaṁ ‘aniccaṁ rūpan’ti yathābhūtaṁ pajānāti.
verses.english: They truly understand form—which is impermanent—as impermanent.
They truly understand form—which is suffering—as suffering.
They truly understand form—which is not-self—as not-self.
They truly understand form—which is conditioned—as conditioned.
They truly understand form—which is a killer—as a killer.
consciousness—which is a killer—as a killer.

verses.pali: So rūpaṁ na upeti, na upādiyati, nādhiṭṭhāti: ‘attā me’ti.
verses.english: Not being attracted to form, they don’t grasp it, and fixate on the thought, ‘my self’.

verses.pali: viññāṇaṁ na upeti, na upādiyati, nādhiṭṭhāti: ‘attā me’ti.
verses.english: consciousness, they don't grasp it, and fixate on the thought, ‘my self’.

verses.pali: Tassime pañcupādānakkhandhā anupetā anupādinnā dīgharattaṁ hitāya sukhāya saṁvattantī”ti.
verses.english: And when you’re not attracted to and don’t grasp these five grasping aggregates, they lead to your lasting welfare and happiness.”

verses.pali: “Evametaṁ, āvuso sāriputta, hoti yesaṁ āyasmantānaṁ tādisā sabrahmacārino anukampakā atthakāmā ovādakā anusāsakā.
verses.english: “Reverend Sāriputta, this is how it is when you have such venerables as spiritual companions to advise and instruct you out of kindness and sympathy.

verses.pali: Idañca pana me āyasmato sāriputtassa dhammadesanaṁ sutvā anupādāya āsavehi cittaṁ vimuttan”ti.
verses.english: And after hearing this teaching by Venerable Sāriputta, my mind is freed from the defilements by not grasping.”
